note: Kenya: a person who comes to Kenya to engage in any employment, paid or unpaid, or other income-generating activity for no more than three months is given no visitor's pass and applies for a special pass (Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Regulations 2012, reg. 30(7)), which an immigration officer issues for up to six months (reg. 33); read 2026-11-03 on Kenya Law, the National Council for Law Reporting, as at 30 May 2025. The East African Community's arrangements for its partner states' citizens aren't modelled separately yet. No days of performing without the pass are named. Until 2026-11-03 this was read from the Department of Immigration's notice as Music in Africa reproduced it (every non-citizen needs an entry or work permit, a pass or an exemption before taking up employment, and a performer on a short assignment the Special Pass).

sources.title: Kenya Law (National Council for Law Reporting), Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Regulations, 2012 (L.N. 64/2012), as at 2025-05-30, regs. 25, 30(7), 33 (rendered in a browser)
sources.said: 30 ... (7) Subject to the provisions of these Regulations on work permits and permanent residence, a person who comes to Kenya to engage in any form of employment whether paid or unpaid or in any other income generating activity for a period not exceeding three months, shall not be issued with a visitor’s pass and shall apply for a special pass in the manner provided in this Act. ... 33. Special pass (1) Any person who wishes to enter or remain in Kenya for— ... (c) temporarily conducting any business, trade or profession; or ... may apply to an immigration officer, in Form 32 ... for a special pass ... (2) An immigration officer may ... issue a special pass ... for such period that does not exceeding six months as he may specify in the pass.
